01_panadol_paracetamol_500.txt.adult: 1–2 tablets (500–1000 mg) every 4–6 hours as needed. Maximum usually 4 g paracetamol/24 h (do not exceed pack maximum; typically ≤8×500 mg/day). Space doses ≥4 hours.
01_panadol_paracetamol_500.txt.child: Do not use adult 500 mg tablets under 12 years unless a doctor advises a weight-based plan. Prefer paediatric suspensions/syrups dosed by weight (≈10–15 mg/kg/dose).
01_panadol_paracetamol_500.txt.pregnancy: Paracetamol is widely used in pregnancy at the lowest effective dose for the shortest time when needed. Avoid chronic high-dose use without medical advice.
01_panadol_paracetamol_500.txt.lactation: Compatible with breastfeeding at usual short-course analgesic doses; amounts in milk are small.
01_panadol_paracetamol_500.txt.sources: GSK Panadol Advance class labeling; standard paracetamol SmPC

02_panadol_cold_flu_day.txt.strength: Paracetamol 500 mg + caffeine 25 mg + phenylephrine HCl 5 mg (ME Day formula)
02_panadol_cold_flu_day.txt.adult: Adults and adolescents ≥12 y: typically 2 tablets every 4–6 hours while symptoms last. Do not exceed pack maximum (commonly 6–8 tablets/24 h). Max course usually a few days.
02_panadol_cold_flu_day.txt.child: Not for children under 12 years (decongestant + combination cold product).
02_panadol_cold_flu_day.txt.pregnancy: Avoid unless a doctor advises: phenylephrine/sympathomimetic decongestants are generally not preferred in pregnancy; combination cold products often labeled do-not-use/ask doctor.
02_panadol_cold_flu_day.txt.lactation: Ask a doctor/pharmacist. Decongestants may reduce milk supply; prefer single-ingredient options when possible.
02_panadol_cold_flu_day.txt.sources: Panadol ME Cold & Flu Day product page; GSK cold/flu leaflets

03_panadol_sinus_relief_pe.txt.adult: Adults/adolescents ≥12 y: usually 2 tablets every 4–6 hours as needed; respect pack maximum (commonly ≤8 tablets/24 h).
03_panadol_sinus_relief_pe.txt.child: Not for under 12 years unless labeled otherwise.
03_panadol_sinus_relief_pe.txt.pregnancy: Avoid phenylephrine decongestant combinations in pregnancy unless clinician-directed.
03_panadol_sinus_relief_pe.txt.lactation: Ask clinician; decongestants may reduce milk supply.
03_panadol_sinus_relief_pe.txt.sources: GSK Panadol Sinus PE class labeling

51_panadol_extra.txt.adult: Adults/adolescents ≥12 y: typically 2 tablets every 4–6 hours as needed. Do not exceed pack maximum (commonly 8 tablets/24 h). Space ≥4 hours. Distinct from Panadol Advance (no caffeine).
51_panadol_extra.txt.pregnancy: Prefer plain paracetamol when possible; caffeine-containing analgesics — ask obstetric advice for more than occasional use.
51_panadol_extra.txt.lactation: Usually compatible short courses; caffeine passes into milk — avoid near bedtime feeds if infant is sensitive.
51_panadol_extra.txt.sources: GSK Panadol Extra class labeling; caffeine+paracetamol SmPC

52_panadol_joint.txt.strength: Paracetamol extended-release joint pain formula (Panadol Joint class)
52_panadol_joint.txt.adult: Adults: follow pack (often 2 tablets every 8 hours for sustained relief). Do not crush/chew modified-release tablets. Max per pack/24 h; do not stack with other paracetamol products.
52_panadol_joint.txt.child: Adult joint modified-release products are not for children.
52_panadol_joint.txt.pregnancy: Paracetamol at lowest effective dose/shortest time when needed; prefer standard immediate-release unless doctor advises otherwise.
52_panadol_joint.txt.sources: GSK Panadol Joint / Osteo class labeling

53_panadol_migraine.txt.strength: Paracetamol + caffeine (+/− other migraine co-actives per SKU)
53_panadol_migraine.txt.adult: Adults: take at migraine onset per pack (commonly 2 tablets). Do not exceed labeled maximum/24 h. Do not combine with other paracetamol or high-caffeine products.
53_panadol_migraine.txt.child: Not for children unless a specific paediatric migraine product is labeled.
53_panadol_migraine.txt.pregnancy: Ask obstetric advice before caffeine-combination migraine analgesics; prefer single-ingredient options when possible.
53_panadol_migraine.txt.lactation: Short courses usually OK; watch infant caffeine sensitivity.

54_panadol_acute_head_cold.txt.strength: Paracetamol + antihistamine + decongestant (Acute Head Cold combo)
54_panadol_acute_head_cold.txt.adult: Adults/≥12 y: typically 2 tablets every 4–6 hours while symptoms last; respect pack max; no other paracetamol products.
54_panadol_acute_head_cold.txt.child: Not for under 12 years (adult cold combo).
54_panadol_acute_head_cold.txt.pregnancy: Avoid multi-ingredient cold products in pregnancy unless clinician-directed.
54_panadol_acute_head_cold.txt.lactation: Avoid if possible (sedation + milk-supply effects from antihistamine/decongestant).
54_panadol_acute_head_cold.txt.sources: GSK Panadol Acute Head Cold class labeling

55_panadol_cold_flu_all_in_one.txt.strength: Multi-symptom Cold & Flu All-In-One (paracetamol + decongestant +/− antihistamine/expectorant per pack)
55_panadol_cold_flu_all_in_one.txt.adult: Adults/≥12 y: dose as on pack (often 2 tablets every 4–6 h). Short courses only; do not duplicate actives across brands.
55_panadol_cold_flu_all_in_one.txt.pregnancy: Avoid combination cold/flu products unless doctor advises.
55_panadol_cold_flu_all_in_one.txt.sources: GSK Panadol Cold & Flu All In One class labeling

56_panadol_vapour_release.txt.strength: Cold & Flu with vapour-release / menthol sensory actives + paracetamol class
56_panadol_vapour_release.txt.adult: Adults/≥12 y: follow pack tablet schedule; do not exceed maxima; avoid stacking other paracetamol cold brands.
56_panadol_vapour_release.txt.child: Not for young children; respect pack age cut-off.
56_panadol_vapour_release.txt.pregnancy: Avoid combination cold products with decongestants in pregnancy unless advised.
56_panadol_vapour_release.txt.lactation: Ask clinician; decongestants may reduce milk supply.
56_panadol_vapour_release.txt.sources: GSK Panadol Cold & Flu Vapour Release class labeling

04_cetal_cold_flu_day.txt.adult: Adults: typically 1–2 tablets every 6–8 hours as needed; do not exceed pack maximum or duplicate other paracetamol products. Limit short courses.
04_cetal_cold_flu_day.txt.child: Usually not for young children; follow Egyptian pack age cut-off (often ≥12 y for adult cold combos).
04_cetal_cold_flu_day.txt.pregnancy: Avoid: pseudoephedrine and first-generation antihistamines in combination cold products are generally not recommended in pregnancy without specialist advice.
04_cetal_cold_flu_day.txt.lactation: Avoid or ask pharmacist: chlorpheniramine may sedate infant; pseudoephedrine can reduce milk supply.
04_cetal_cold_flu_day.txt.sources: Egyptian cold-combo class labeling; pseudoephedrine pregnancy/lactation cautions

05_flurest_n.txt.adult: Adults: usually 1 tablet every 6–8 hours as needed; do not exceed pack maximum; do not combine with other paracetamol products.
05_flurest_n.txt.child: Age-restricted; not for infants/young children — use paediatric formulations if prescribed.
05_flurest_n.txt.pregnancy: Avoid combination cold products with phenylephrine/antihistamine unless doctor advises.
05_flurest_n.txt.lactation: Avoid if possible (sedating antihistamine + decongestant effects on milk supply).
05_flurest_n.txt.sources: GSK Flurest-N catalog actives + cold-product class SmPC cautions

06_congestal.txt.adult: Adults: typically 1 tablet 3 times daily or as on pack; max short course; no other paracetamol.
06_congestal.txt.child: Follow pack minimum age; adult tablets not for young children.
06_congestal.txt.pregnancy: Avoid pseudoephedrine-containing cold products in pregnancy unless clinician-directed.
06_congestal.txt.lactation: Avoid/ask: may reduce milk supply and sedate infant.

07_sine_up.txt.adult: Adults: 1 tablet every 6–8 hours as needed per pack; avoid duplicate actives.
07_sine_up.txt.child: Not for young children; respect pack age limit.

08_bradozen.txt.adult: Dissolve 1 lozenge slowly in the mouth every 2–4 hours (commonly 3–6 times/day). Do not chew/swallow whole. Do not exceed pack daily maximum.
08_bradozen.txt.child: Not for infants (choking risk). For school-age children only if pack allows; dissolve slowly under supervision.
08_bradozen.txt.pregnancy: Topical antiseptic with minimal systemic absorption; ask doctor/pharmacist before use (standard lozenge warning).
08_bradozen.txt.lactation: Likely low systemic exposure; ask clinician before routine use.
08_bradozen.txt.sources: Medizen Bradozen; Health Canada throat-lozenge monograph (domiphen)

09_notussil.txt.strength: Cloperastine HCl 20 mg/5 ml suspension (Egyptian Notussil note) / class 3.54 mg/ml syrups elsewhere
09_notussil.txt.adult: Egyptian Notussil-type: adults often 5 ml three times daily (confirm concentration on bottle). EU cloperastine 3.54 mg/ml syrups commonly 10 ml three times daily for ≥12 y.
09_notussil.txt.child: Contraindicated under 2 years. Age-banded syrup dosing (examples for 3.54 mg/ml class): 2–4 y 2 ml BID; 5–6 y 3 ml BID; 7–12 y 5 ml BID–TID — always follow the Egyptian pack.
09_notussil.txt.pregnancy: Contraindicated / not recommended — insufficient human data (AEMPS/EU SmPC).
09_notussil.txt.lactation: Not recommended; unknown excretion in milk (EU SmPC).
09_notussil.txt.sources: Notussil Egypt pack notes; AEMPS CIMA Cloperastine Kern SmPC

10_tussigreen.txt.strength: Corpus proxy: benproperine cough syrup class (Tussiglobe catalog match); confirm real Tussigreen PIL if available
10_tussigreen.txt.adult: Benproperine class: adults often 25–50 mg 2–3 times daily OR syrup tablespoon-equivalent 2–3×/day with meals (Egyptian Pectipro-class leaflets).
10_tussigreen.txt.child: Age-banded syrup teaspoons (example Pectipro-class): 1–3 y ½ tsp; 3–6 y 1 tsp; 6–12 y 2 tsp; 2–3× daily. Catalog min.age for Tussiglobe proxy: 6 years.
10_tussigreen.txt.sources: Benproperine monograph; Egyptian Pectipro syrup leaflet class

11_daflon_500.txt.adult: Venous insufficiency: 2 tablets daily (1 midday + 1 evening) with meals. Acute hemorrhoids: 6 tablets/day for 4 days then 4 tablets/day for 3 days (Servier SmPC).
11_daflon_500.txt.pregnancy: Prefer avoid as precaution — limited human data; animal studies not teratogenic (Servier).
11_daflon_500.txt.lactation: Not recommended — unknown if excreted in milk (Servier).

12_daflon_1000.txt.adult: Usual: 1 tablet daily with a meal. Acute hemorrhoids: 3 tablets/day ×4 days then 2 tablets/day ×3 days (Servier SmPC).

13_controloc_20.txt.adult: Typical GERD/symptomatic acid: 20 mg once daily before meal for short courses (often 2–4 weeks) or as prescribed. Higher doses for ulcer/H. pylori per doctor.
13_controloc_20.txt.child: Specialist paediatric dosing only; not routine OTC for young children.
13_controloc_20.txt.pregnancy: Generally considered acceptable if acid suppression needed (PPI class; use when benefit outweighs risk).
13_controloc_20.txt.lactation: Small amounts may appear in milk; usually compatible for short courses — confirm with clinician.

14_jeparilon.txt.strength: Famotidine 10 mg + calcium carbonate + magnesium hydroxide chewable (Pepcid Complete–class)
14_jeparilon.txt.adult: Chew 1 tablet completely when symptoms occur; do not swallow whole. Max 2 tablets/24 h. Limit short self-care courses (≈2 weeks) unless doctor advises.
14_jeparilon.txt.child: Typically ≥12 years (US OTC class). Not for younger children unless prescribed.
14_jeparilon.txt.pregnancy: Ask doctor before use; combination lacks adequate pregnancy studies — use only if benefit outweighs risk.
14_jeparilon.txt.sources: DailyMed Pepcid Complete; HPRA Pepcid Duo SmPC class

15_anaseziago.txt.adult: Intact skin minor procedures: apply thick layer under occlusive dressing, typically ~1.5 g/10 cm² for ~1 hour (follow pack). Do not apply to broken skin/eyes/mucosa unless directed.
15_anaseziago.txt.child: Strict max dose/area/time by age & weight (e.g. 0–3 mo ≤1 g/10 cm²/1 h; older children higher per EMLA table). Avoid in <37 weeks gestation neonates; caution with methemoglobin-inducing drugs in infants <12 mo.
15_anaseziago.txt.pregnancy: Former FDA Cat B; use only if clearly needed (limited human data).
15_anaseziago.txt.lactation: Small milk amounts; EMC states can be used if clinically needed at therapeutic topical doses.

16_adol_500.txt.adult: 1–2 tablets every 4–6 h PRN; max usually 4 g/24 h.
16_adol_500.txt.child: Prefer paediatric liquid under 12 y; weight-based 10–15 mg/kg/dose.
16_adol_500.txt.pregnancy: Preferred simple analgesic in pregnancy at lowest effective dose/shortest time.

17_cataflam_25.txt.strength: Catalog match Cataflam 50 mg sugar-coated (diclofenac potassium); file name legacy 25 mg
17_cataflam_25.txt.adult: Diclofenac potassium: often 50 mg initially then 25–50 mg every 6–8 h as needed; max commonly 150 mg/day short course with food. Use lowest dose/shortest duration.
17_cataflam_25.txt.child: Not for young children unless specialist paediatric diclofenac product prescribed.
17_cataflam_25.txt.pregnancy: Avoid in 3rd trimester (ductus arteriosus / oligohydramnios risk). Avoid if possible in 1st/2nd unless doctor directs.
17_cataflam_25.txt.lactation: Prefer avoid NSAIDs or use short courses only with clinician advice; ibuprofen often preferred if NSAID needed.
17_cataflam_25.txt.sources: Diclofenac potassium SmPC; Novartis Cataflam class

18_brufen_400.txt.adult: 200–400 mg every 6–8 h with food; OTC max often 1200 mg/day; prescription regimens may go higher under supervision.
18_brufen_400.txt.child: Use paediatric ibuprofen by weight (~5–10 mg/kg/dose). Adult 400 mg tablets not for young children.
18_brufen_400.txt.pregnancy: Avoid in 3rd trimester; avoid if possible earlier unless advised.
18_brufen_400.txt.lactation: Usually compatible in short courses at usual doses; prefer after feeds if concerned.

19_antinal.txt.adult: Common adult regimen: 200 mg four times daily for acute bacterial diarrhoea short courses (typically ≤7 days) — follow pack/doctor.
19_antinal.txt.child: Age/formulation dependent; suspensions for younger children when labeled. Capsules not for toddlers.
19_antinal.txt.pregnancy: Avoid unless clinician judges benefit > risk (limited data for nifuroxazide).
19_antinal.txt.lactation: Ask clinician; often avoided if safer alternatives exist.

20_flagyl_500.txt.adult: Indication-dependent (e.g. anaerobic infection / amebiasis / bacterial vaginosis protocols). Common oral ranges 400–500 mg 2–3×/day for prescribed durations. Avoid alcohol during and ≥48 h after.
20_flagyl_500.txt.child: Weight-based paediatric dosing only under prescription.
20_flagyl_500.txt.pregnancy: Avoid in 1st trimester if possible; may be used later when clearly indicated (e.g. trichomoniasis protocols) under obstetric advice.
20_flagyl_500.txt.lactation: Excreted in milk; may interrupt breastfeeding for high-dose courses or choose alternatives — follow obstetric/paediatric advice.

21_augmentin_1g.txt.strength: Amoxicillin 875 mg + clavulanate 125 mg (1 g co-amoxiclav)
21_augmentin_1g.txt.adult: Typically 1 tablet every 12 hours with food for prescribed duration (often 5–14 days). Complete the course.
21_augmentin_1g.txt.child: Use paediatric suspensions by weight; adult 1 g tabs not for young children.
21_augmentin_1g.txt.pregnancy: Penicillins generally considered acceptable when antibiotic needed.
21_augmentin_1g.txt.lactation: Usually compatible; watch infant for diarrhoea/rash/thrush.

22_hibiotic_1g.txt.adult: Usually 1 g every 12 h with food for the prescribed course.
22_hibiotic_1g.txt.lactation: Usually compatible; monitor infant GI symptoms.

23_zithrokan_500.txt.adult: Common short courses: 500 mg once daily for 3 days, OR 500 mg day 1 then 250 mg days 2–5 — indication-specific.
23_zithrokan_500.txt.child: Weight-based paediatric regimens; capsules may not suit young children.
23_zithrokan_500.txt.pregnancy: Macrolides used when indicated; azithromycin often acceptable with clinician oversight.
23_zithrokan_500.txt.lactation: Usually compatible short courses; monitor infant GI flora.

24_ciprobay_500.txt.adult: Often 500 mg every 12 h for prescribed duration. Separate from dairy/antacids/minerals by ≥2–4 h. Tendon/CNS warnings apply.
24_ciprobay_500.txt.child: Generally avoid in children/adolescents unless specialist exception (cartilage risk).
24_ciprobay_500.txt.pregnancy: Avoid if safer alternatives exist (fluoroquinolone caution).

25_risek_20.txt.adult: Usually 20 mg once daily before breakfast for GERD/ulcer regimens as prescribed (duration often 2–8 weeks).
25_risek_20.txt.lactation: Small milk amounts; usually compatible short courses.

26_gaviscon.txt.adult: Typically 10–20 ml after meals and at bedtime (follow bottle). Do not exceed pack maximum.
26_gaviscon.txt.child: Age-banded paediatric alginate products preferred; adult Advance may be ≥12 y.
26_gaviscon.txt.pregnancy: Alginates widely used for pregnancy heartburn when lifestyle measures fail.

27_motilium_10.txt.adult: Often 10 mg up to 3 times daily before meals; short courses preferred. Cardiac QT risk — respect max daily dose and contraindications.
27_motilium_10.txt.child: Restricted; cardiac risk — specialist only / avoid in young children per current warnings.
27_motilium_10.txt.pregnancy: Use only if clearly needed; limited data.
27_motilium_10.txt.lactation: Used carefully (also galactagogue off-label) — cardiac risk assessment required; prefer clinician oversight.

28_buscopan.txt.strength: Catalog match Buscopan Plus (hyoscine butylbromide + analgesic combo) / Buscopan class
28_buscopan.txt.adult: Hyoscine butylbromide class: often 10–20 mg up to 3–4×/day. Buscopan Plus: follow combo pack (includes analgesic) — do not exceed labeled maxima.
28_buscopan.txt.pregnancy: Ask doctor; anticholinergics used with caution.

29_concor_5.txt.adult: Hypertension/HF titration under doctor — common maintenance 2.5–10 mg once daily. Do not stop abruptly.
29_concor_5.txt.pregnancy: Beta-blockers may be used when indicated; fetal growth monitoring may be needed — specialist care.
29_concor_5.txt.lactation: Bisoprolol: limited data; monitor infant for bradycardia/hypoglycaemia if used.

30_norvasc_5.txt.adult: Usually 5 mg once daily (may titrate to 10 mg). Take consistently.
30_norvasc_5.txt.pregnancy: Calcium-channel blockers may be used when needed under obstetric advice.
30_norvasc_5.txt.lactation: Amlodipine appears in milk in small amounts; often considered acceptable with monitoring.

31_glucophage_500.txt.adult: Start often 500 mg once/twice daily with meals; titrate as tolerated. Typical maintenance 1500–2000 mg/day in divided doses (max per local label).
31_glucophage_500.txt.pregnancy: Increasingly used in GDM/PCOS under obstetric protocols; follow specialist advice.

32_amaryl_2.txt.adult: Usually start 1 mg once daily with breakfast; titrate. Maintenance often 1–4 mg/day (max commonly 6–8 mg). Hypoglycaemia risk.
32_amaryl_2.txt.pregnancy: Avoid sulfonylureas; switch to insulin protocols in pregnancy.

33_lipitor_20.txt.adult: Usually 10–20 mg once daily (range 10–80 mg) at any time of day. Avoid grapefruit excess.

34_plavix_75.txt.adult: Maintenance 75 mg once daily. Loading doses for ACS only under cardiology protocols.
34_plavix_75.txt.pregnancy: Use only if clearly needed (bleeding risk).

35_aspocid_75.txt.adult: Antiplatelet: 75–100 mg once daily as prescribed. Take with food if GI upset.
35_aspocid_75.txt.child: Avoid aspirin in children/teens with viral illness (Reye risk) unless specialist Kawasaki protocols.
35_aspocid_75.txt.pregnancy: Low-dose aspirin used in obstetric protocols when indicated; avoid analgesic-dose NSAID aspirin especially late pregnancy.

36_telfast_120.txt.adult: Allergic rhinitis: 120 mg once daily. Chronic urticaria may use 180 mg products.
36_telfast_120.txt.child: Age-banded paediatric fexofenadine; 120 mg tabs usually ≥12 y.
36_telfast_120.txt.pregnancy: Non-sedating antihistamines: use if needed after clinician advice (fexofenadine often acceptable).
36_telfast_120.txt.lactation: Limited data; non-sedating agents preferred over 1st-generation — ask pharmacist.

37_claritine_10.txt.child: Paediatric syrups/chewables by age; 10 mg tabs often ≥6–12 y per label.
37_claritine_10.txt.pregnancy: Often considered acceptable non-sedating choice when antihistamine needed.
37_claritine_10.txt.lactation: Usually compatible; amounts in milk low.

38_otrivin_0_1.txt.adult: Usually 2–3 drops per nostril up to 2–3 times daily. Max continuous use typically 3–5–7 days to avoid rebound congestion.
38_otrivin_0_1.txt.child: 0.1% is adult strength — use 0.05% paediatric products for children per age label.
38_otrivin_0_1.txt.pregnancy: Prefer short courses / saline first; systemic absorption possible — ask obstetric advice.
38_otrivin_0_1.txt.lactation: Short topical courses usually low concern; prefer saline if possible.

39_ventolin_inhaler.txt.adult: Relief: typically 1–2 puffs as needed; may repeat. Acute severe asthma needs medical emergency care. Controllers are separate.
39_ventolin_inhaler.txt.child: Paediatric puff counts by age/spacer; caregiver training essential.
39_ventolin_inhaler.txt.pregnancy: Salbutamol inhalers are used in pregnancy when needed for asthma control — uncontrolled asthma is riskier.

40_singulair_10.txt.adult: 10 mg once daily in the evening.
40_singulair_10.txt.child: Age-specific chewable/granule strengths (4–5 mg); 10 mg for ≥15 y typically.
40_singulair_10.txt.pregnancy: Use if benefit outweighs risk; asthma control priority.
40_singulair_10.txt.lactation: Limited data — usually continue if clinically needed with monitoring.

41_diflucan_150.txt.adult: Vaginal candidiasis: single 150 mg oral dose (common). Other infections need multi-day regimens.
41_diflucan_150.txt.child: Weight-based systemic regimens when prescribed — not the single 150 mg OTC pattern.
41_diflucan_150.txt.pregnancy: Avoid single/high-dose fluconazole in pregnancy especially 1st trimester (teratogenicity signals at high/prolonged doses).
41_diflucan_150.txt.lactation: Compatible after single 150 mg dose in many references; confirm for multi-day courses.

42_lamisil_250.txt.adult: Often 250 mg once daily for weeks–months depending on nail/skin infection site.
42_lamisil_250.txt.pregnancy: Prefer postpone oral terbinafine until after pregnancy unless essential.
42_lamisil_250.txt.lactation: Avoid oral terbinafine — excreted in milk.

43_duphaston_10.txt.adult: Indication-specific (cycle support, endometriosis, threatened miscarriage protocols): commonly 10 mg 2–3×/day for defined days — only as prescribed.
43_duphaston_10.txt.pregnancy: Used in obstetric protocols when prescribed; do not self-medicate.
43_duphaston_10.txt.lactation: Progestogens may be used with caution — follow obstetric advice.

44_folic_acid_5.txt.adult: Deficiency/therapeutic: often 5 mg daily. Preconception neural-tube prevention commonly 400 mcg–5 mg depending on risk (high-risk 5 mg).
44_folic_acid_5.txt.pregnancy: Recommended in pregnancy; higher doses for high-risk women under advice.
44_folic_acid_5.txt.sources: Folic acid SmPC / WHO antenatal guidance class

45_ferrotron.txt.adult: Usually 1 capsule daily or as pack directs, preferably not with tea/coffee/calcium/quinolones at the same moment (space 2–4 h).
45_ferrotron.txt.child: Adult iron capsules not for young children (overdose risk).
45_ferrotron.txt.pregnancy: Iron supplementation common in pregnancy when indicated — follow antenatal dose.
45_ferrotron.txt.sources: Oral iron counseling standards; Ferrotron pack class

46_milga.txt.adult: Often 1 tablet 1–3 times daily as labeled for vitamin B supplementation/neuropathy support.
46_milga.txt.child: Adult strengths usually not for young children.
46_milga.txt.pregnancy: B vitamins generally acceptable at physiologic doses; avoid megadoses unless advised.
46_milga.txt.sources: Vitamin B complex counseling; Eva Milga pack class

47_smecta.txt.adult: Often 3 sachets/day (or suspension equivalent) between meals for acute diarrhoea short courses; ensure rehydration.
47_smecta.txt.child: Age-banded sachets; maintain ORS. Not a substitute for rehydration.
47_smecta.txt.pregnancy: Generally considered acceptable (minimal absorption) when needed.

48_enterogermina.txt.adult: Typically 1–2 mini-bottles/day (or as pack), spaced from antibiotics by a few hours when possible.
48_enterogermina.txt.child: Paediatric schedules on pack; widely used in children when labeled.
48_enterogermina.txt.pregnancy: Probiotics generally considered low risk; use labeled products.

49_strepsils.txt.strength: Antiseptic/local anaesthetic lozenges (Honey & Lemon catalog match)
49_strepsils.txt.adult: Dissolve 1 lozenge slowly every 2–3 hours as needed; respect max/day on pack.
49_strepsils.txt.child: Choking risk — usually ≥6 years if pack allows; never for infants.
49_strepsils.txt.pregnancy: Short topical courses generally acceptable; check specific actives (amylmetacresol/dichlorobenzyl alcohol etc.).
49_strepsils.txt.lactation: Short courses usually fine; avoid excessive use.

50_comtrex.txt.strength: Multi-ingredient cold tablet (paracetamol + antihistamine + decongestant class)
50_comtrex.txt.adult: Typically 1–2 tablets every 6 hours as needed; do not exceed pack max; no other paracetamol products.
50_comtrex.txt.pregnancy: Avoid combination cold products; prefer single-ingredient clinician-guided options.
50_comtrex.txt.lactation: Avoid if possible (sedation + milk-supply effects from antihistamine/decongestant).
50_comtrex.txt.sources: Comtrex Acute Head Cold class labeling
